content.text: I've reviewed the fees, pricing, revenue-sharing, term, grant and cooperation provisions. No take-or-pay or volume commitment binds us.

input.quote: 4.1 License Fees. In consideration for the licenses granted to Corio pursuant to Section 2 of this Agreement, Corio shall pay the license fees specified in EXHIBIT B hereto.
input.rationale: This meets the preferred position: there is no minimum purchase commitment, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty imposed on us (Corio, the licensee/customer). Section 4 charges only license fees, annual maintenance and support fees, and taxes; Exhibit B prices the licence, MarketSite.net access, maintenance, revenue share and time-and-materials implementation (the latter capped, in our favour), and the revenue-share fees in p0157–p0160 accrue only on actual Corio Customer revenue once a Customer goes live. There are no volume caps on our usage either — Software Users are "Unlimited" (p0151) and Section 2.1(iv) permits sublicensing an unlimited number of Customers. The only quasi-volume language, the "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" in p0158, operates inside a carve-out that relieves us of revenue-share on the initial 3000 licences, so it benefits us. Exhibit D is expressly "non-binding" and the initial-customers item (p0205) is a commercially reasonable efforts undertaking, not a purchase commitment. Noted but not flagged: the term is five years (Section 11.1) with annual MarketSite.net access and maintenance fees and no termination-for-convenience right; maintenance is, however, expressly conditioned on our continuing to elect to pay it (Sections 4.2 and 11.3), so this is a subscription fee structure rather than a multi-year take-or-pay commitment. No redline required.
